**Video:** [Lec 33 — Regularization](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7F8pknXk_-o)

## Learning goals

- Define **regularization** as techniques that **increase bias** (to reduce variance).
- Write **parameter-penalty** regularized ERM ($\ell_2$ / $\ell_1$).
- See $\lambda$ as a **hyperparameter** (validation), not something you must dualize away.

## Before this clicks

Small samples + high capacity $\Rightarrow$ overfitting (low bias, high variance). Data often live near a thin **manifold** in a huge ambient $\mathbb{R}^{d}$; explaining every wiggle on that tiny set creates brittle decision boundaries. We need controlled bias.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Definition used in this course

> **Regularization** = any technique that **increases the bias** of the hypothesis.

Goal is still low risk: raise bias a bit to cut variance a lot when $n$ is limited.

### 2. Why overfitting is easy on thin manifolds

Images-as-vectors occupy a tiny subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. ERM that insists on fitting that cloud tightly builds partitions that do not move with the cloud — huge variance on a shifted test sample. Underfitting refuses to explain the cloud at all. Regularization navigates between these.

### 3. Parameter-penalty regularized ERM

$$
\min_\theta\;
\widehat{R}(\theta)+\lambda\,\Omega(\theta).
$$

Common choices:

| $\Omega(\theta)$ | Name (linear models) | Effect (intuition) |
|------------------|----------------------|--------------------|
| $\|\theta\|_2^{2}$ | **Ridge** | Shrinks weights smoothly (“low-frequency” preference) |
| $\|\theta\|_1$ | **Lasso** | Encourages sparsity |
| $\|\theta\|_0$ | counts nonzeros | Ideal sparsity, but not a norm / not differentiable |

For polynomial regression, penalizing $\|\theta\|_2$ discourages huge high-degree coefficients that memorize points.

Constrained form $\min \widehat{R}$ s.t. $\Omega(\theta)\le t$ is related by Lagrange multipliers; ML practice usually **fixes $\lambda$** on validation data rather than solving a full primal–dual search for $\lambda$.

### 4. Other regularization families (preview)

1. Parameter penalties (today).
2. **Optimization** procedures (early stopping — next lectures).
3. **Architectural** restrictions (CNNs as regularized MLPs — later).

### 5. Design note

Any differentiable penalty you like is allowed in principle (even exotic shapes); differentiability matters because we optimize numerically. $\ell_0$ needs subgradients / combinatorial tricks.

---

## Worked mini-example

Degree-$10$ polynomial on $n=10$ points: unpenalized ERM can interpolate. Add $\lambda\|\theta\|_2^{2}$ with large $\lambda$: coefficients shrink, curve smooths, training error rises a bit, test error often falls — classic bias up / variance down.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Regularization always means $\ell_2$ | $\ell_2$ is one penalty; architecture and early stopping also regularize. |
| Larger $\lambda$ always better | Too large $\Rightarrow$ underfit; tune on validation. |
| Lasso / ridge names swapped | $\ell_1$ lasso, $\ell_2$ ridge. |
